title: Rigveda 3.21: To Agni
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 3.21: To Agni: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 3.21 is a hymn of 5 verses addressed to Agni. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 3, the family book of Viśvāmitra. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 203r-203v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 3.21.1-5 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 1, varga 21); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 203v
translation.original_text:
1i̱maṁ no̍ ya̱jñam a̱mṛte̍ṣu dhehī̱mā ha̱vyā jā̍tavedo juṣasva | sto̱kānā̍m agne̱ meda̍so ghṛ̱tasya̱ hota̱ḥ prāśā̍na pratha̱mo ni̱ṣadya̍ ||
2ghṛ̱tava̍ntaḥ pāvaka te sto̱kāḥ śco̍tanti̱ meda̍saḥ | svadha̍rman de̱vavī̍taye̱ śreṣṭha̍ṁ no dhehi̱ vārya̍m ||
3tubhya̍ṁ sto̱kā ghṛ̍ta̱ścuto 'gne̱ viprā̍ya santya | ṛṣi̱ḥ śreṣṭha̱ḥ sam i̍dhyase ya̱jñasya̍ prāvi̱tā bha̍va ||
4tubhya̍ṁ ścotanty adhrigo śacīvaḥ sto̱kāso̍ agne̱ meda̍so ghṛ̱tasya̍ | ka̱vi̱śa̱sto bṛ̍ha̱tā bhā̱nunāgā̍ ha̱vyā ju̍ṣasva medhira ||
5oji̍ṣṭhaṁ te madhya̱to meda̱ udbhṛ̍ta̱m pra te̍ va̱yaṁ da̍dāmahe | ścota̍nti te vaso sto̱kā adhi̍ tva̱ci prati̱ tān de̍va̱śo vi̍hi ||
translation.text:
1SET this our sacrifice among the Immortals: be pleased with these our presents, Jâtavedas. O Priest, O Agni, sit thee down before us, and first enjoy the drops of oil and fatness.
2For thee, O Purifier, flow the drops of fatness rich in oil. After thy wont vouchsafe to us the choicest boon that Gods may feast.
3Agni, Most Excellent! for thee the Sage are drops that drip with oil. Thou art enkindled as the best of Seers. Help thou the sacrifice.
4To thee, O Agni, mighty and resistless, to thee stream forth the drops of oil and fatness. With great light art thou come, O praised by poets! Accept our offering, O thou Sage.
5Fatness exceeding rich, extracted from the midst,– this as our gift we offer thee. Excellent God, the drops run down upon thy skin. Deal them to each among the Gods.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 203v (numbered 13v by the scribe) (OPenn image 205, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 3.21.1 ‹agne medasaḥ ghṛtasya hotariti›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 204r (numbered 14r by the scribe), begins in RV 3.22.1 ‹sutam dadhe jaṭhare vāvaśānaḥ›. Verses 3.21.1-5 end on this page; 3.21.1 begins on fol. 203r (numbered 13r by the scribe).
